dial.summary: BTC.D holding at 59.3% with perpetual funding rates near zero (0.0031%) confirm continuing spot-driven accumulation; DXY headwind persists at 102.21 (above 100) and real yields hold at 2.87%, but the 2s10s curve steepens to +44bps and the October 14 CPI print — now 3 days away — is the single macro catalyst that could reprice DXY and real yields and unlock the next BTC leg higher.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) confirmed at $103,649B per StreetStats Oct 9 data; 4-week trend flat — no new September G4 data yet (6–8 week reporting lag); YoY growth positive so status neutral — confirmed rising 4-week trend required for supportive; next G4 M2 update expected mid-November 2026.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: September 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI = 54.5% (released Oct 1, 2026; August 54.6%, 4-week change −0.1pp within flat threshold); New Orders 55.3%, Prices Paid 77.9% (highest since mid-2021); status neutral — above 50 but not rising on 4-week basis; next release November 2, 2026 for October data.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY spot closed at 102.21 on October 9, 2026 (Trading Economics 102.2264, CNBC 102.231, DealPlexus 102.21; Oct 10 Saturday, Oct 12 Columbus Day holiday — next live session Oct 13); 4-week trend up from ~99.9 on Sep 9 (+~2.3%); status headwind (above 100 threshold); October 14 CPI is the key repricing catalyst — miss below 3.0% YoY required for DXY break below 100.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: DFII10 at 2.87% as of October 8, 2026 (last confirmed FRED observation; StreetStats intraday Oct 9 showed 2.89% unconfirmed; next FRED release Oct 13 post-Columbus Day holiday); 4-week trend up from ~2.52% on Sep 8 (+~35bps); status headwind (rising on 4-week basis and above 2% threshold); October 14 CPI is the key repricing catalyst.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: October 9, 2026: 10Y at 5.24%, 2Y at 4.80% → spread = +44bps (per ETF Trends/Forbes Treasury snapshot; Columbus Day Oct 12 means next live session Oct 13); 4-week trend up (steepening from ~+42bps on Sep 9 to +44bps); status supportive (positive and steepening on 4-week basis — both criteria met); FOMC Oct 27–28 and Oct 14 CPI are the next major curve catalysts.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL at $6,747,560M ($6.748T) for week ending October 7, 2026 (H.4.1, released Oct 8; next release Oct 15 covering week ending Oct 14); 4-week trend flat: Sep 9 ~$6,737B → Oct 7 $6,748B = +$11B (+0.16%); status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau, no QT acceleration).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: Carried forward from Oct 9, 2026 reading (Binance BTCUSDT perp at 0.0031% per 8h; coinglass.com DNS unreachable Oct 11); 4-week trend down from MacroMicro Sep 30 cross-exchange avg of 0.0067% to 0.0031% on Oct 9; BTC at ~$82,800 (Oct 10 prediction market mid); status supportive (well below 0.04% overheating threshold — confirms spot-driven accumulation, not leveraged speculation).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Carried forward from Oct 9, 2026 reading (coingecko.com DNS unreachable Oct 11); stablecoin market cap ~$308B vs total crypto ~$2.81T (tv-hub BTC.D 59.3%, Oct 9); 30-day trend flat: ~10.4–10.6% (Sep 9) → ~10.7% (Oct 9) = marginal rise within flat threshold; status neutral (not clearly falling on 30-day basis; headwind condition not confirmed).

upcoming.title: CPI (September 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Consumer Price Index for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — the dominant macro catalyst before the October 27–28 FOMC; August CPI YoY was ~3.4%; ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid at 77.9% is a leading upside signal; a hot print above +3.5% YoY would revive October hike odds and push DXY above 104, while a miss below +3.0% YoY would cement Fed hold expectations and potentially catalyze a BTC breakout from the current accumulation range.

upcoming.title: PPI (September 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Producer Price Index for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — pipeline inflation released the day after CPI; released alongside Retail Sales and Initial Jobless Claims, making October 15 the most data-dense pre-FOMC morning; a hot PPI following a hot CPI would reinforce October hike expectations and likely drive DXY back toward 104; ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid at 77.9% is a leading signal for potential upside.

upcoming.title: Retail Sales (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Retail Sales for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — given the September NFP shock (+29K), a weak retail sales print would confirm broad economic softening and reinforce a Fed hold narrative; a strong print alongside weak labor extends the late-cycle bifurcation signal (resilient consumer, softening employment); provides key pre-FOMC context on Q3 consumer demand ahead of the October 29 GDP advance estimate.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended October 11, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for the week ended October 11, 2026 — released alongside September PPI and Retail Sales; claims trajectory directly informs market odds for a Fed pause vs. hike at the October 27–28 meeting; a print above 200K would reinforce labor market softening following the September NFP shock of +29K.

upcoming.title: Fed Balance Sheet H.4.1 (week ended October 14, 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve H.4.1 weekly balance sheet release at 4:30 PM ET — covers week ending October 14, 2026; prior reading $6,747,560M ($6.748T, week ending Oct 7); four consecutive weeks of flat-to-marginal expansion; a shift toward contraction combined with rising overnight rates would flip status from supportive to headwind.

upcoming.title: Industrial Production & Capacity Utilization (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Board releases September 2026 Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization at 9:15 AM ET; completes the Q3 output picture ahead of the GDP advance estimate (October 29); September ISM Manufacturing at 54.5% and Production Index at 56.7% suggest solid output growth; a miss would reinforce stagflation risk narrative (hot prices, softening activity) into the October 27–28 FOMC.
